Landslide Data from Southern Ecuador.

Source: R/data.R
landslides.Rd

Data on landslides in a region of Ecuador.

Usage

landslides

Format

An sf object with an WGS 84 / UTM zone 17S point projection with 349 rows and 8 columns:

  • landslide_ind: an indicator variable that is a 0 if a landslide did not take place at the location and a 1 if a landslide did take place.

  • landslide_fct: a factor with two levels: no if a landslide did not take place and yes if a landslide did take place.

  • slope: the angle of the slope, in degrees.

  • cplan: plan curvature. This is a measure of how the terrain bends across a slope, in radians per meter, and is a commonly used metric for water flow.

  • cprof: profile curvature, in radians per meter, a measure of flow acceleration.

  • elev: elevation, in meters above sea level.

  • log10_carea: the base-10 logarithm of the catchment area, a measure of the amount of water flowing toward a location.

  • geometry: point-level geometry of the locations.

Source

Data were modified from the spDataLarge R package and the RSAGA R package. The data are used in the "Statistical learning for geographic data" chapter of the Geocomputation with R book (https://r.geocompx.org/spatial-cv.html. The data appear in the published works listed in the references below.

References

Muenchow, J., Brenning, A., Richter, R. (2012): Geomorphic process rates of landslides along a humidity gradient in the tropical Andes, Geomorphology 139-140, 271-284. DOI: 10.1016/j.geomorph.2011.10.029. Stoyan, R. (2000): Aktivitaet, Ursachen und Klassifikation der Rutschungen in San Francisco/Suedecuador. Unpublished diploma thesis, University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, Germany.
